title: The competency ratchet predicts no planarian mutant strains with abnormal morphology

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The competency ratchet predicts no planarian mutant strains with abnormal morphology

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The competency-ratchet model predicts, and it is the case, that there are no known mutant planarian strains with abnormal morphologies (unlike flies or mice), explains the difficulty of making transgenic planaria, and the only known permanent abnormal planarian lines (two-headed and randomized 1- vs 2-head forms) arose from bioelectric rather than genetic change.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › An evolutionary intelligence ratchet

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For example, it predicts the confirmed fact that there are no known mutant planarian strains with abnormal morphologies (the way there are for fruit flies, mice, etc.) and explains why the research community has had such a hard time (despite decades of efforts) generating transgenic planaria.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “An evolutionary intelligence ratchet”. Scope: Planarians compared with Drosophila, mice and other model organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The absolute 'no known strain' statement is searchable and readily falsified, and transgenesis attempts can be catalogued. Publication bias and unequal technical effort prevent those observations from decisively confirming the competency-ratchet mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Systematically search planarian strain, mutant, and transgenesis records for heritable abnormal morphology, classify genetic versus physiological origins, and compare discovery effort with established model organisms. A verified genetic strain with stable abnormal morphology refutes the absolute prediction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Planarian research effort and genetic tools differ from fly and mouse.

Absence of reports is not proof of absence.

The claimed explanation is not uniquely predicted by the observation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.58
data existence: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.76
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The contrast with flies and mice is directly queryable in phenotype databases, and planarian strain reports are public literature. That is enough to test a claim about what is known, including the bioelectric origin of the familiar two-headed lines. It is not a complete census of stocks, and the competency-ratchet explanation of the absence is not tested by the search.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Search FlyBase, Mouse Genome Informatics, and the planarian literature for stable inherited strains whose anatomy differs from wild type in the absence of ongoing RNAi or drug treatment. Morphological mutant strains in flies and mice, and at least one published planarian strain of that kind, would refute the negative planarian clause; a documented absence of such planarian strains, with the only permanent abnormal lines being the bioelectric one-head and two-head forms, would support it as a statement about the public record.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A literature search can refute the negative claim by finding a strain, but cannot prove that no unpublished strain exists.

RNAi phenotypes and transient drug phenotypes are easy to mistake for mutant strains.

Transgenesis attempts after the paper's publication can change the public record without a single dedicated database.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.7
